decisive_items: a left periprosthetic soft‐tissue mass measuring 9 × 8 × 10 cm, without bony involvement or bone‐marrow edema
persistent buttock pain and intermittent electric shock–like sensations radiating down the left leg
Serum cobalt and chromium levels were within normal limits
response.rationale: The large periprosthetic soft-tissue mass with pain and no infection (negative cultures) favors adverse local tissue reaction (ALTR) over metallosis, which is contradicted by normal cobalt/chromium levels. Infection is less likely given negative cultures and only mild inflammatory markers.

rejected.why: Negative cultures and lack of systemic symptoms argue against infection despite elevated joint fluid white cells.
Normal serum cobalt and chromium levels contradict metallosis in a ceramic-on-ceramic bearing.
Chronic infection is not supported by negative cultures and only mild inflammatory response.
Tendinosis cannot explain the large periprosthetic mass.
Osteolysis is contradicted by unchanged radiographs and no bony involvement on MRI.
Bursitis is contradicted by progression to radiating neuropathic symptoms and a large mass.
